title: Challenges in Measuring Low Concentration of Overlapping Elements with EDS and Need for Verification with Standard Materials
content: EDS is being used with increasing frequency to characterize materials, including compositional information using quantitative analysis. Careful characterization of energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) efficiency, individual detector optimization, use of built-in factory standard files, accurate determination of peak areas, correct deconvolution, and correction of pile up artifacts, have improved the accuracy and sensitivity of EDS with the aim of providing accurate “out of the box” EDS results [1]. With all the parameters carefully considered EDS quantitative analysis has been shown to achieve high accuracy equivalent to that of wavelength dispersive x-ray spectrometry (WDS) even in the case of highly overlapped X-ray peaks of major elements [2] and separately high precision even in the case of trace elements with concentrations below 1 wt.% [3]. With reliable pulse pile-up correction, accurate, unnormalized EDS quantification was also demonstrated at count rates above 200 kcps [4,5]. The challenge put forward in this work is to evaluate EDS quantification of trace elements which X-ray peaks severely overlapped X-ray peaks of major elements at high count rates, with the aim of improving the productivity of these measurements. A proven way to check the accuracy of quantitative results is by comparison with well-characterized standards of known composition. While several mineral, glass and alloy standards exist to verify the quantification of major elements, it is more problematic to find well-defined standards containing minor and trace elements whose X-ray peak overlaps with other peaks.
